lensName: Prof. Warren Sack lens: recursive social systems
rationale: The recurring method is plainly stated on About and reconstructable through three bounded projects with actual historical or current social use. The pages connect relationships to models, interfaces, public or collective use, and continuing documentation. Dated past work is treated as evidence of method; the current research lab and WOWList return are not used to invent completed client adoption.

individuallyAssessableRequirements.evidence: WOWList, Sunday Dinner/196, and NYCAC/FairRentNYC each supply the five-stage trace below. Dated past work is included under the owner's clarification.

individuallyAssessableRequirements.requirement: One visible surface within two clicks states the recursive method plainly and links to evidence.

individuallyAssessableRequirements.requirement: Social structure and information architecture connect to usable interfaces, participation, learning, and handoffs.
individuallyAssessableRequirements.evidence: Organizer vocabulary becomes keyword communities; hospitality becomes invitation/onboarding/space/access workflows; coalition questions become public action paths and recoverable decisions.

evidence.finding: The plain-language recursive sequence and linked project comparisons supply a usable entry point.
The method and examples remain readable in the mobile column.
A connected product narrative runs from Sunday Dinner calendars through keyword communities to organizer use and public support.
The two redacted workflows expose sequence and handoff form without publishing private records.
The public-system, working-alignment, and public-room sequence connects information architecture to collective use and ongoing records.

The 2016 issue interface, 61 issue pages, public repository, documented Council-account interactions, and archive disclaimer add bounded prototype evidence. I do not need to treat Council engagement as proof of resident adoption to satisfy the three-project requirement.
The proposed sprint, synthetic example, historical correction trace, human review, and explicit absence of established client adoption remain distinct.

threeProjectTrace.dates: 2014 provenance, 2015 independent tutorial, 2016 public support, July 2017 production snapshot; current 2026 return is only a threshold.
threeProjectTrace.observeRelationships: Sunday Dinner calendars and DIY organizers reveal communities organized by interests, places, venues, scenes, and informal networks.
threeProjectTrace.modelSystem: Collaboratively editable natural-language event text and followable keyword communities translate that social vocabulary into a distribution model.
threeProjectTrace.prototypeInterface: The co-built web service connects publishing, profiles, followed lists, calendars, and weekly email.
threeProjectTrace.socialUseAndLearning: Independent organizers published a tutorial and linked local calendars through the system; the 2016 Sunday Dinner event links to its WOWList event page. Historical public support explains how real organizers join and publish.
threeProjectTrace.documentHandoff: Public support material, organizer tutorials, reusable publishing/distribution patterns, and the bounded historical record make participation and continuation inspectable.
threeProjectTrace.boundary: These sources establish dated workflows and bounded organizer use, not a formal research protocol, complete adoption census, current service availability, or sole authorship.

threeProjectTrace.dates: Public gathering milestones 2014 and 2016; documented residency workflow 2023 and recurring operating sheet 2025.
threeProjectTrace.observeRelationships: Hosting and artist support start from hospitality, trust, shared space, returning participants, and an orientation conversation about the artist's and collaborator's needs.
threeProjectTrace.modelSystem: The work joins invitations, responses, preparation, attendance/follow-up, space configuration, access, and continued support into explicit repeatable workflows.
threeProjectTrace.prototypeInterface: The redacted public specimens expose the operating-sheet logic and the receive/orient/configure/hand-off/remain-available sequence. The interfaces include invitations, the room, onboarding, and independent access.
threeProjectTrace.socialUseAndLearning: The record supports real recurring gatherings and an accepted artist/collaborator workflow, with needs made discussable and changes supported. It does not claim an artist outcome or that every residency followed this exact process.
threeProjectTrace.documentHandoff: Minimal continuity records, follow-up, practical orientation, and independent-access knowledge enable the next gathering and the resident's day-to-day work while private values remain withheld.
threeProjectTrace.boundary: This is evidence of a used social operating method, not formal usability testing, participant consent to renewed publication, or verified artistic impact.

threeProjectTrace.modelSystem: The architecture separates supported public sources, protected context, unresolved questions, decisions, next actions, and city/state lanes in recoverable campaign memory.
